## What the cell pins (one paragraph)

KS-922 (#971) fixed the Stage-1 JOIN at `orchestrate.sh:119` to the bash-3.2-safe `${stage1_pids[@]+"${stage1_pids[@]}"}` form, and CELL 14 (`:433-443`) guards it by the ABSENCE of the false sentence "a Stage-1 job exited non-zero" when zero Stage-1 jobs start. The ticket's fix shape is to require `Stage 1 JOIN complete` in that run's output. This brief adds it as its OWN cell, directly after the stage1-absent run and before CELL 14 reads the output, so CELL 14 itself is unchanged.

The six `+` lines go between `rc_s1absent="$(run_orchestrator …)"` (`:434`) and `out_s1absent="$(cat …)"` (`:435`). Copy every line byte for byte. The `+` lines are ASCII only (a plain `-` in the cell description, never a dash character), contain no backslash and no bash-4 idiom, and there is no blank line in the fence. Keep the header exactly as shown.

+# KS-1134: CELL 14 below asserts an ABSENCE, so a run that DIES before the Stage-1 JOIN passes it too (the gate's Tg).
+if grep -q 'Stage 1 JOIN complete' "$WORK/s1absent/out.txt"; then

+fi

```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# TESTS for Blockchain/Testing/ci/orchestrate.sh — job dispatch (KS-868)
# =============================================================================
# The defect: every Stage-1 job was guarded by `[ -x "$TESTING/jobs/$job.sh" ]`
# with no `else`. All nine jobs are tracked 100644, so on any clone that
# condition was FALSE for every one — the orchestrator started nothing, said
# nothing, and went on to report success having executed no security job.
# Two more, in the same file: SELF was assigned and never exported, and RUN_DIR
# was never set at all, while the nine jobs read them 18 and 50 times under
# `set -u`. And the post-API loop reported a job that never ran as having
# "exited non-zero" — wrong, in the direction that reads as "we tried".
#
# NOT the suite's subject: `run-internal-audit.sh` is the DOCUMENTED entry point
# and it was never broken — it invokes jobs as `bash "$script"` with RUN_DIR and
# SELF passed explicitly, which is why it is immune to all four. A cell below
# pins that invocation shape so a future "fix" cannot make the working path
# depend on the mode bit.
#
# The fixture runs the REAL orchestrate.sh end to end. Two tricks make that fast
# and hermetic: the API gate is satisfied by a `file://` TARGET_BASE (curl -fsS
# succeeds on an existing file, fails on a missing one — both measured), and the
# Stage-2 tool and the aggregator are stubs inside the fixture's own ci/.
#
# Usage: bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/orchestrate_jobs.test.sh
#        ORCH_SH=/path/to/other/orchestrate.sh bash …   (red-proof)
# =============================================================================
set -uo pipefail
export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../../../.." && pwd)"
# KS-923 F2 — `${ORCH_SH:-…}` treats SET-BUT-EMPTY as unset, so `ORCH_SH=""`
# fell back to the SHIPPED orchestrator and printed a green run byte-identical
# to a genuine one, with nothing in the output naming which file it graded. A
# red-proof harness that can silently grade the wrong subject is worse than no
# harness. Three changes: the colon is dropped, set-but-empty is refused
# explicitly, and EVERY run names its subject and that subject's hash.
if [ "${ORCH_SH+set}" = set ] && [ -z "$ORCH_SH" ]; then
  echo "FATAL: ORCH_SH is set but EMPTY — refusing to silently grade the shipped orchestrator." >&2
  exit 2
fi
ORCH="${ORCH_SH-$REPO_ROOT/Blockchain/Testing/ci/orchestrate.sh}"
JOBS_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/Blockchain/Testing/jobs"
AUDIT_RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/Blockchain/Testing/run-internal-audit.sh"

[ -f "$ORCH" ] || { echo "FATAL: orchestrate.sh not found at $ORCH" >&2; exit 2; }
# KS-941 QA-923-1 — EXISTENCE IS NOT READABILITY, forty lines below a comment
# saying so. `[ -f ]` is true for a mode-000 subject; before this guard the
# `shasum` below wrote "Permission denied" to stderr and the SUBJECT line went
# out with an EMPTY sha256 — the identifying field #869 added so a transcript
# could be trusted to name what it graded — then the run went on to a loud,
# mis-attributed verdict. Refused here, before anything is printed about it.
[ -r "$ORCH" ] || { echo "FATAL: ORCH_SH is not readable at $ORCH" >&2; exit 2; }
printf 'SUBJECT %s\n        sha256 %s\n\n' "$ORCH" "$(shasum -a 256 "$ORCH" | cut -d" " -f1)"

WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks868.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

pass=0; fail=0; skipped=0
ok()  { printf '  ok   %s\n' "$1"; pass=$((pass + 1)); }
bad() { printf '  FAIL %s\n     %s\n' "$1" "$2"; fail=$((fail + 1)); }
# KS-941 QA-923-2 — a cell that did NOT run is neither a pass nor a failure.
# It used to be printed through ok(), so a leaked KS923_SELFTEST_CHILD produced
# "12 passed, 0 failed" with eleven cells measured. Counted apart, printed apart.
skip() { printf '  skip %s\n' "$1"; skipped=$((skipped + 1)); }

# Build a fixture Testing/ tree around the orchestrator under test.
# $1 = dir. $2 = "all" | "one-missing" (job 02 removed).
build_fixture() {
  # $2 = all | one-missing | one-unreadable | post-api-unreadable   (job condition)
  #      | stage1-absent | stage1-one-failing                         (KS-922, CELLS 14/15)
  # $3 = exec | noexec | absent | failing | badshebang | unreadable  (Stage-2 tool)
  local root="$1" mode="$2" stage2="${3:-exec}" j job_rc
  rm -rf "$root"; mkdir -p "$root/Testing/ci/tools" "$root/Testing/jobs" "$root/api"
  cp "$ORCH" "$root/Testing/ci/orchestrate.sh"
  echo ok > "$root/api/health"
  # Stage-2 tool and aggregator: stubs, so the run reaches its own exit code.
  #
  # KS-923: $3 varies the Stage-2 tool and NOTHING ELSE, one condition per cell —
  #   exec (default) | noexec (present, 100644) | absent | failing (runs, exits 3)
  # A single fixture that tripped several of these at once would measure the
  # bundle and say nothing about the parts. The stub RECORDS that it ran, because
  # "the tool executed" cannot be read off the orchestrator's exit code: that was
  # 0 in every one of these states before the fix, which is why this went unseen.
  if [ "$stage2" != absent ]; then
    # KS-923 F4: `badshebang` names an interpreter that does not exist. A
    # BARE-PATH call fails at execve with ENOENT and the script never runs; a
    # `bash "$p"` call reads the file and treats the shebang as a comment, so it
    # DOES run. That is a behavioural discriminator for the invocation shape,
    # which a source grep is not.
    { if [ "$stage2" = badshebang ]; then printf '#!/nonexistent/interpreter-ks923\n'
      else printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\n'; fi
      printf 'printf "ran\\n" >> "%s/stage2_ran.txt"\n' "$root"
      if [ "$stage2" = failing ]; then printf 'exit 3\n'; else printf 'exit 0\n'; fi
    } > "$root/Testing/ci/tools/run-schemathesis.sh"
    case "$stage2" in
      noexec)     chmod 644 "$root/Testing/ci/tools/run-schemathesis.sh" ;;
      # KS-923 F1: present and executable, but NOT READABLE. `[ ! -f ]` is false
      # here, so the pre-F1 guard passed and bash then failed on permission.
      unreadable) chmod 000 "$root/Testing/ci/tools/run-schemathesis.sh" ;;
      *)          chmod +x  "$root/Testing/ci/tools/run-schemathesis.sh" ;;
    esac
  fi
  printf 'process.exit(0);\n' > "$root/Testing/ci/aggregate.ts"
  # Job stubs in the real jobs' shape: `set -u`, `cd "$SELF"`, reading RUN_DIR.
  # Deliberately 100644 on disk — the defect's precondition. A dispatcher that
  # needs the mode bit cannot run these.
  for j in 01-dependency-audit 02-secret-scan 03-sast-semgrep 04-container-trivy \
           06-tenant-isolation 07-license-compliance 08-aiken-tests; do
    [ "$mode" = one-missing ] && [ "$j" = 02-secret-scan ] && continue
    # KS-922: `stage1-absent` leaves EVERY Stage-1 job absent and keeps only
    # 06-tenant-isolation (post-API), so Stage 1 is the one thing that varies:
    # stage1_pids stays EMPTY and the JOIN loop meets an empty array.
    [ "$mode" = stage1-absent ] && [ "$j" != 06-tenant-isolation ] && continue
    # KS-922: `stage1-one-failing` keeps every job and makes ONE Stage-1 job
    # exit 3 — the control that the "exited non-zero" sentence is still said
    # when it is true.
    job_rc=0
    [ "$mode" = stage1-one-failing ] && [ "$j" = 02-secret-scan ] && job_rc=3
    cat > "$root/Testing/jobs/$j.sh" <<JOB
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail
cd "\$SELF"
printf '%s|SELF=%s|RUN_DIR=%s\n' "$j" "\$SELF" "\$RUN_DIR" >> "$root/ran.txt"
exit $job_rc
JOB
    # KS-923 F1: `one-unreadable` makes ONE Stage-1 job mode-000, so the shared
    # readability guard is DRIVEN on the Stage-1 path too and not merely inferred
    # from the Stage-2 cell.
    if [ "$mode" = one-unreadable ] && [ "$j" = 02-secret-scan ]; then
      chmod 000 "$root/Testing/jobs/$j.sh"
    # KS-936: `post-api-unreadable` makes 06-tenant-isolation mode-000. That job
    # is reachable ONLY from the post-API loop (orchestrate.sh:125); Stage 1's
    # list at :104 does not contain it. So this fixture drives the post-API path
    # and nothing else — the path CELL 11 left inferred.
    elif [ "$mode" = post-api-unreadable ] && [ "$j" = 06-tenant-isolation ]; then
      chmod 000 "$root/Testing/jobs/$j.sh"
    else
      chmod 644 "$root/Testing/jobs/$j.sh"
    fi
  done
}

run_orchestrator() {
  local root="$1"
  ( cd "$root/Testing/ci" \
    && TIER=pr TARGET_BASE="file://$root/api" FINDINGS_DIR="$root/.findings" \
       bash "$root/Testing/ci/orchestrate.sh" ) >"$root/out.txt" 2>&1
  echo $?
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 1 — the census. All nine job scripts must be tracked 100755. A spot check
# would pass on one file; the defect was that ALL nine were 100644.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
modes="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" ls-files -s Blockchain/Testing/jobs/ | awk '{print $1}' | sort -u)"
count="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" ls-files Blockchain/Testing/jobs/ | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
if [ "$count" -eq 0 ]; then
  bad "the nine job scripts are tracked 100755 (census)" "git ls-files matched NOTHING — the census cannot see the jobs"
elif [ "$modes" = "100755" ]; then
  ok "all $count tracked job scripts are 100755 in the INDEX (census over every one, not a sample)"
else
  bad "all tracked job scripts are 100755 in the INDEX" "modes present: $(echo "$modes" | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 2 — CONTROL. A fixture where every job is present runs CLEAN. Without
# this, the refusal cell below could pass by refusing everything.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/all" all
rc_all="$(run_orchestrator "$WORK/all")"
ran_all=0; [ -f "$WORK/all/ran.txt" ] && ran_all="$(wc -l < "$WORK/all/ran.txt" | tr -d ' ')"
if [ "$rc_all" = 0 ] && [ "$ran_all" -eq 7 ]; then
  ok "CONTROL — every job present: the run exits 0 and all 7 fixture jobs RAN"
else
  bad "CONTROL — every job present: the run exits 0 and all 7 fixture jobs RAN" \
      "rc=$rc_all, jobs that ran=$ran_all, output: $(tail -3 "$WORK/all/out.txt" | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 3 — SELF and RUN_DIR must be BOUND IN A CHILD, i.e. exported and not
# merely set. The stubs run under `set -u` and open with `cd "$SELF"`, so an
# unexported variable kills them; CELL 2 already proves they ran.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [ -f "$WORK/all/ran.txt" ] \
   && ! grep -q 'SELF=|' "$WORK/all/ran.txt" && ! grep -q 'RUN_DIR=$' "$WORK/all/ran.txt" \
   && grep -q 'SELF=/' "$WORK/all/ran.txt" && grep -q 'RUN_DIR=/' "$WORK/all/ran.txt"; then
  ok "SELF and RUN_DIR are BOUND in a child process — exported, not merely set"
else
  bad "SELF and RUN_DIR are BOUND in a child process" \
      "recorded: $(head -2 "$WORK/all/ran.txt" 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ' || echo '<no job ran>')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 4 — THE REGRESSION. One job script missing: the run must REFUSE loudly,
# name the job, and exit NON-ZERO. A run that could not start a security job has
# not passed its gate (KS-676 / KS-854: an empty result is not a pass).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/miss" one-missing
rc_miss="$(run_orchestrator "$WORK/miss")"
out_miss="$(cat "$WORK/miss/out.txt")"
if [ "$rc_miss" != 0 ] && printf '%s' "$out_miss" | grep -q 'REFUSED' \
   && printf '%s' "$out_miss" | grep -q '02-secret-scan'; then
  ok "a missing job makes the run REFUSE loudly, BY NAME, and exit non-zero (rc=$rc_miss)"
else
  bad "a missing job makes the run REFUSE loudly, BY NAME, and exit non-zero" \
      "rc=$rc_miss, REFUSED present=$(printf '%s' "$out_miss" | grep -qc 'REFUSED' && echo yes || echo no), output: $(tail -4 "$WORK/miss/out.txt" | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 5 — DO NOT REGRESS THE WORKING PATH. run-internal-audit.sh must keep
# invoking jobs as `bash "$script"` with RUN_DIR and SELF passed explicitly.
# That is why it was never broken, and a "fix" that made the jobs depend on
# being directly executable would break the documented entry point to repair a
# draft. Pinned as a literal, with a control that the file is readable at all.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [ ! -f "$AUDIT_RUNNER" ]; then
  bad "run-internal-audit.sh still passes RUN_DIR and SELF and uses bash \"\$script\"" \
      "the file is not at $AUDIT_RUNNER — the cell cannot check what it is named for"
elif grep -q 'RUN_DIR="\$RUN_DIR" SELF="\$SELF"' "$AUDIT_RUNNER" && grep -q 'bash "\$script"' "$AUDIT_RUNNER"; then
  ok "the WORKING path is intact — run-internal-audit.sh still passes RUN_DIR + SELF and runs jobs via bash"
else
  bad "run-internal-audit.sh still passes RUN_DIR and SELF and uses bash \"\$script\"" \
      "the documented entry point's invocation shape changed; it must not come to depend on the mode bit"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 6 — KS-923. THE REGRESSION. An ABSENT Stage-2 tool must REFUSE by name
# and exit non-zero. Measured on the merged tip a821bd0aa BEFORE the fix: rc 0,
# "Stage 2 JOIN complete", and the gate printing pass — a security-tool dispatch
# path that could not report its own absence.
#
# Asserted on the ABSENCE of the false sentence, not on the exit code: once the
# refusal lands the exit code is non-zero for that reason alone, so it cannot
# tell "did not run" from "ran and failed". CELL 9 is the control proving the
# sentence still appears when it is true.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/s2absent" all absent
rc_s2absent="$(run_orchestrator "$WORK/s2absent")"
out_s2absent="$(cat "$WORK/s2absent/out.txt")"
if [ "$rc_s2absent" != 0 ] \
   && printf '%s' "$out_s2absent" | grep -q 'REFUSED' \
   && printf '%s' "$out_s2absent" | grep -q "Stage-2 tool 'schemathesis' has no script" \
   && ! printf '%s' "$out_s2absent" | grep -q 'a Stage-2 tool exited non-zero'; then
  ok "an ABSENT Stage-2 tool REFUSES by name and exits non-zero, and does NOT claim it exited non-zero (rc=$rc_s2absent)"
else
  bad "an ABSENT Stage-2 tool REFUSES by name, exits non-zero, and claims nothing about having run" \
      "rc=$rc_s2absent, output: $(tail -5 "$WORK/s2absent/out.txt" | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 7 — KS-923. The mode bit must NOT be load-bearing. A Stage-2 tool present
# but tracked 100644 must still RUN. Proven by the stub's own record, because
# the orchestrator exited 0 in this state before the fix too.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/s2mode" all noexec
rc_s2mode="$(run_orchestrator "$WORK/s2mode")"
if [ "$rc_s2mode" = 0 ] && [ -f "$WORK/s2mode/stage2_ran.txt" ]; then
  ok "a Stage-2 tool tracked 100644 still RUNS — invoked via bash, so the mode bit is not load-bearing"
else
  bad "a Stage-2 tool tracked 100644 still RUNS" \
      "rc=$rc_s2mode, tool ran=$([ -f "$WORK/s2mode/stage2_ran.txt" ] && echo yes || echo NO), output: $(tail -4 "$WORK/s2mode/out.txt" | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 8 — KS-923 F4. BEHAVIOURAL proof of the invocation shape, replacing a
# source grep. The stub's shebang names an interpreter that does not exist: a
# bare-path call fails at execve with ENOENT and the script never runs, while
# `bash "$p"` reads the file and treats the shebang as a comment, so it runs.
#
# The grep this replaces had ZERO unique coverage over CELL 7 and was wrong in
# both directions — a bare-path reversion leaving the literal in a COMMENT kept
# it green, and a cosmetic `bash "${SC_TOOL}"` reddened it. No source pin is
# kept: this cell measures the property directly, so a second, weaker statement
# of it would only add a way to be wrong.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/s2shebang" all badshebang
rc_shebang="$(run_orchestrator "$WORK/s2shebang")"
if [ -f "$WORK/s2shebang/stage2_ran.txt" ]; then
  ok "the Stage-2 tool RUNS with a nonexistent interpreter in its shebang — it is invoked via bash, not by bare path"
else
  bad "the Stage-2 tool is invoked via bash, not by bare path" \
      "the stub never ran (rc=$rc_shebang) — a bare-path call fails at execve when the shebang names no real interpreter"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 9 — CONTROL for CELL 6. A Stage-2 tool that genuinely RAN and exited
# non-zero must STILL report "exited non-zero", and must not fail the run —
# the message is correct in this state. Without this, CELL 6 could pass because
# the sentence is never emitted at all, which would make it blind rather than
# discriminating.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/s2fail" all failing
rc_s2fail="$(run_orchestrator "$WORK/s2fail")"
out_s2fail="$(cat "$WORK/s2fail/out.txt")"
if [ "$rc_s2fail" = 0 ] && [ -f "$WORK/s2fail/stage2_ran.txt" ] \
   && printf '%s' "$out_s2fail" | grep -q 'a Stage-2 tool exited non-zero'; then
  ok "CONTROL — a Stage-2 tool that RAN and failed DOES report 'exited non-zero' (so CELL 6 discriminates), and does not fail the run"
else
  bad "CONTROL — a Stage-2 tool that RAN and failed reports 'exited non-zero' and does not fail the run" \
      "rc=$rc_s2fail, tool ran=$([ -f "$WORK/s2fail/stage2_ran.txt" ] && echo yes || echo NO), output: $(tail -4 "$WORK/s2fail/out.txt" | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 10 — KS-923 F1. An UNREADABLE Stage-2 tool must refuse. `[ ! -f ]` is
# FALSE for a mode-000 file, so before F1 the guard passed, bash failed on
# permission, and the run said "a Stage-2 tool exited non-zero" about a tool
# that never ran — byte-for-byte the pre-fix verdict, one state over.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/s2unread" all unreadable
S2_UNREAD_TOOL="$WORK/s2unread/Testing/ci/tools/run-schemathesis.sh"
if [ -r "$S2_UNREAD_TOOL" ]; then
  # Running as root defeats mode-000. Say so rather than pass: a cell that
  # cannot discriminate must not report ok.
  bad "an UNREADABLE Stage-2 tool REFUSES by name and exits non-zero" \
      "the mode-000 fixture is STILL READABLE (running as root?) — this cell cannot discriminate and is not reporting a pass"
else
  rc_unread="$(run_orchestrator "$WORK/s2unread")"
  out_unread="$(cat "$WORK/s2unread/out.txt")"
  if [ "$rc_unread" != 0 ] \
     && printf '%s' "$out_unread" | grep -q 'NOT READABLE' \
     && printf '%s' "$out_unread" | grep -q "Stage-2 tool 'schemathesis'" \
     && ! printf '%s' "$out_unread" | grep -q 'a Stage-2 tool exited non-zero'; then
    ok "an UNREADABLE Stage-2 tool REFUSES by name and exits non-zero, and does NOT claim it exited non-zero (rc=$rc_unread)"
  else
    bad "an UNREADABLE Stage-2 tool REFUSES by name, exits non-zero, and claims nothing about having run" \
        "rc=$rc_unread, output: $(tail -5 "$WORK/s2unread/out.txt" | tr '\n' ' ')"
  fi
fi
chmod 644 "$S2_UNREAD_TOOL" 2>/dev/null

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 11 — KS-923 F1 on the STAGE-1 path. require_job() delegates to the same
# require_script(), so one fix covers three call sites — but "covers" is a claim
# until a second path is DRIVEN. This drives Stage 1; only the post-API loop
# (06-tenant-isolation) remains inferred, and the READY says so.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/s1unread" one-unreadable
S1_UNREAD_JOB="$WORK/s1unread/Testing/jobs/02-secret-scan.sh"
if [ -r "$S1_UNREAD_JOB" ]; then
  bad "an UNREADABLE Stage-1 job REFUSES by name and exits non-zero" \
      "the mode-000 fixture is STILL READABLE (running as root?) — this cell cannot discriminate"
else
  rc_s1unread="$(run_orchestrator "$WORK/s1unread")"
  out_s1unread="$(cat "$WORK/s1unread/out.txt")"
  if [ "$rc_s1unread" != 0 ] \
     && printf '%s' "$out_s1unread" | grep -q 'NOT READABLE' \
     && printf '%s' "$out_s1unread" | grep -q '02-secret-scan'; then
    ok "an UNREADABLE Stage-1 job REFUSES by name and exits non-zero — the shared guard is DRIVEN on this path, not inferred (rc=$rc_s1unread)"
  else
    bad "an UNREADABLE Stage-1 job REFUSES by name and exits non-zero" \
        "rc=$rc_s1unread, output: $(tail -5 "$WORK/s1unread/out.txt" | tr '\n' ' ')"
  fi
fi
chmod 644 "$S1_UNREAD_JOB" 2>/dev/null

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 12 — KS-923 F2. The harness must REFUSE a set-but-empty ORCH_SH rather
# than falling back to the shipped file and printing a green run that looks
# exactly like a genuine one. Re-invokes THIS suite with ORCH_SH="" and requires
# a non-zero exit. KS923_SELFTEST_CHILD stops the child re-entering this cell,
# so a regression here cannot fork forever.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [ "${KS923_SELFTEST_CHILD:-0}" = 1 ]; then
  skip "CELL 12 skipped in the self-test child (recursion guard held)"
else
  ORCH_SH="" KS923_SELFTEST_CHILD=1 bash "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" >"$WORK/selftest.out" 2>"$WORK/selftest.err"
  rc_empty=$?
  if [ "$rc_empty" -ne 0 ] && grep -q 'set but EMPTY' "$WORK/selftest.err"; then
    ok "ORCH_SH set-but-EMPTY is REFUSED (rc=$rc_empty) instead of silently grading the shipped orchestrator"
  else
    bad "ORCH_SH set-but-EMPTY is REFUSED instead of silently grading the shipped orchestrator" \
        "rc=$rc_empty; stderr: $(head -2 "$WORK/selftest.err" | tr '\n' ' '); stdout head: $(head -2 "$WORK/selftest.out" | tr '\n' ' ')"
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 13 — KS-936. THE GATE MUST NOT PASS on the post-API path.
#
# Why this is not a restatement of CELLS 10 and 11. `require_job` delegates to
# the same `require_script`, so the CODE is shared and CELL 11 already drives it
# on Stage 1. What differs is the OBSERVABLE, and it is the one that matters:
#
#   Stage 1 pre-fix      -> rc NON-ZERO. CELL 11 pins that refusal.
#   post-API loop pre-fix -> rc 0. A GATE PASS, with "06-tenant-isolation exited
#                            non-zero (continuing)" said about a job that never
#                            ran. Nothing pinned that.
#
# A future change that stopped the post-API loop refusing would leave CELLS 10
# and 11 green while a run that could not start a security job reported success.
# That is KS-868, the parent defect, exactly. So this cell asserts THE GATE DOES
# NOT PASS — not merely that a refusal appears somewhere in the output.
#
# It sits after CELL 12 rather than beside CELLS 10/11 so the existing cell
# numbers keep their meaning; KS-941 cites CELL 12 by number.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/postapiunread" post-api-unreadable
PA_UNREAD_JOB="$WORK/postapiunread/Testing/jobs/06-tenant-isolation.sh"
if [ -r "$PA_UNREAD_JOB" ]; then
  # Same precondition guard CELLS 10 and 11 carry: root defeats mode-000, and a
  # cell that cannot discriminate must not report a pass.
  bad "an UNREADABLE post-API job makes the GATE NOT PASS" \
      "the mode-000 fixture is STILL READABLE (running as root?) — this cell cannot discriminate and is not reporting a pass"
else
  rc_pa="$(run_orchestrator "$WORK/postapiunread")"
  out_pa="$(cat "$WORK/postapiunread/out.txt")"
  if [ "$rc_pa" != 0 ] \
     && printf '%s' "$out_pa" | grep -q 'NOT READABLE' \
     && printf '%s' "$out_pa" | grep -q '06-tenant-isolation' \
     && ! printf '%s' "$out_pa" | grep -q '06-tenant-isolation exited non-zero'; then
    ok "an UNREADABLE post-API job makes the GATE NOT PASS (rc=$rc_pa), REFUSES by name, and does NOT claim the job ran — the path CELL 11 left inferred is now DRIVEN"
  else
    bad "an UNREADABLE post-API job makes the GATE NOT PASS, REFUSES by name, and claims nothing about having run" \
        "rc=$rc_pa (rc=0 here is the pre-fix GATE PASS this cell exists to catch), output: $(tail -5 "$WORK/postapiunread/out.txt" | tr '\n' ' ')"
  fi
fi
chmod 644 "$PA_UNREAD_JOB" 2>/dev/null

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 14 — KS-922. THE REGRESSION. When NO Stage-1 job started, the Stage-1
# JOIN must not say "a Stage-1 job exited non-zero". On bash 3.2
# `"${stage1_pids[@]:-}"` expands an EMPTY array to one empty word, so the loop
# ran once with pid="", `wait ""` failed, and the run logged a Stage-1 failure
# about a job that never existed — the "we tried" sentence KS-868 removed from
# the post-API loop and KS-923 removed from Stage 2, eleven lines below the fix.
#
# Asserted on the ABSENCE of the false sentence, not on the exit code: with
# every Stage-1 job refused the exit code is non-zero for that reason alone and
# cannot discriminate. The six refusals are asserted BY NAME-COUNT so the cell
# cannot pass by the run dying before the JOIN. CELL 15 is the control.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/s1absent" stage1-absent
rc_s1absent="$(run_orchestrator "$WORK/s1absent")"
out_s1absent="$(cat "$WORK/s1absent/out.txt")"
refused_s1absent="$(printf '%s\n' "$out_s1absent" | grep -c 'REFUSED — job')"
if [ "$rc_s1absent" != 0 ] && [ "$refused_s1absent" -eq 6 ] \
   && ! printf '%s' "$out_s1absent" | grep -q 'a Stage-1 job exited non-zero'; then
  ok "KS-922 — with ZERO Stage-1 jobs started the JOIN says nothing about a job exiting non-zero (6 refusals, rc=$rc_s1absent)"
else
  bad "KS-922 — with ZERO Stage-1 jobs started the JOIN says nothing about a job exiting non-zero" \
      "rc=$rc_s1absent, refusals=$refused_s1absent, false sentence present=$(printf '%s' "$out_s1absent" | grep -q 'a Stage-1 job exited non-zero' && echo YES || echo no), output: $(grep -v 'REFUSED — job' "$WORK/s1absent/out.txt" | tail -4 | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 15 — CONTROL for CELL 14. A Stage-1 job that genuinely RAN and exited
# non-zero must STILL be reported, exactly once, and must not fail the run —
# the sentence is correct in that state ("continuing" is the design). Without
# this, CELL 14 could pass because the sentence is never emitted at all.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/s1fail" stage1-one-failing
rc_s1fail="$(run_orchestrator "$WORK/s1fail")"
ran_s1fail=0; [ -f "$WORK/s1fail/ran.txt" ] && ran_s1fail="$(wc -l < "$WORK/s1fail/ran.txt" | tr -d ' ')"
said_s1fail="$(grep -c 'a Stage-1 job exited non-zero' "$WORK/s1fail/out.txt")"
if [ "$rc_s1fail" = 0 ] && [ "$ran_s1fail" -eq 7 ] && [ "$said_s1fail" -eq 1 ]; then
  ok "CONTROL — a Stage-1 job that RAN and exited 3 IS reported 'exited non-zero' exactly once (so CELL 14 discriminates), and the run continues (rc=0)"
else
  bad "CONTROL — a Stage-1 job that RAN and exited non-zero is reported exactly once and the run continues" \
      "rc=$rc_s1fail, jobs that ran=$ran_s1fail, sentence count=$said_s1fail, output: $(tail -4 "$WORK/s1fail/out.txt" | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 16 — KS-941 QA-923-1. The harness's OWN subject guard must refuse a
# subject that exists but is NOT READABLE. `[ -f ]` is true for a mode-000
# file, so before the `-r` guard the suite printed a SUBJECT line with an EMPTY
# sha256 — the identifying field #869 added so a transcript could be trusted to
# name what it graded — and ran on to a loud but mis-attributed verdict.
# Re-invokes THIS suite with ORCH_SH pointing at a mode-000 copy and requires
# exit 2, a FATAL naming readability, and NO SUBJECT line. Same root caveat as
# CELLS 10/11/13; same recursion guard as CELL 12.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [ "${KS923_SELFTEST_CHILD:-0}" = 1 ]; then
  skip "CELL 16 skipped in the self-test child (recursion guard held)"
else
  cp "$ORCH" "$WORK/orch_mode000.sh" && chmod 000 "$WORK/orch_mode000.sh"
  if [ -r "$WORK/orch_mode000.sh" ]; then
    bad "an UNREADABLE subject is REFUSED (exit 2, FATAL, no SUBJECT line)" \
        "the mode-000 copy is STILL READABLE (running as root?) — this cell cannot discriminate and is not reporting a pass"
  else
    ORCH_SH="$WORK/orch_mode000.sh" KS923_SELFTEST_CHILD=1 bash "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" >"$WORK/unread.out" 2>"$WORK/unread.err"
    rc_unread_subj=$?
    if [ "$rc_unread_subj" -eq 2 ] && grep -q 'FATAL: ORCH_SH is not readable' "$WORK/unread.err" \
       && ! grep -q '^SUBJECT ' "$WORK/unread.out"; then
      ok "an UNREADABLE subject is REFUSED with exit 2 and a FATAL naming readability, and NO SUBJECT line is printed"
    else
      bad "an UNREADABLE subject is REFUSED (exit 2, FATAL, no SUBJECT line)" \
          "rc=$rc_unread_subj; stderr: $(head -1 "$WORK/unread.err" | cut -c1-120); stdout head: $(head -2 "$WORK/unread.out" | tr '\n' ' ' | cut -c1-160)"
    fi
  fi
  chmod 644 "$WORK/orch_mode000.sh" 2>/dev/null
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 17 — KS-941 QA-923-2. A cell that did NOT run must not be counted as a
# PASS. With KS923_SELFTEST_CHILD leaked in from outside, CELL 12 (and now 16
# and 17) skip — and the totals read "N passed, 0 failed" with rc 0 while N-k
# cells were measured. Re-invokes THIS suite as a child with the variable set
# and the SAME subject, and requires PARITY between the totals line and the
# lines above it — `passed` == the `ok` lines, `failed` == the `FAIL` lines,
# `skipped` == the `skip` lines, at least one skip, none disguised as an ok —
# and, STANDING_LINES rule 2, ruled for KS-941 on 2026-09-13, a NON-ZERO exit,
# because a run that could not execute part of itself has not passed. Parity
# rather than `failed == 0`: a first draft required zero failures in the child,
# which made this cell go red whenever ANY other cell did (measured under the
# CELL 14 tamper) — a cell that repeats every other cell's verdict is not its
# own. The parent's own totals line is the control: a normal run prints
# "... 0 skipped" and exits by its failure count.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [ "${KS923_SELFTEST_CHILD:-0}" = 1 ]; then
  skip "CELL 17 skipped in the self-test child (recursion guard held)"
else
  ORCH_SH="$ORCH" KS923_SELFTEST_CHILD=1 bash "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" >"$WORK/leak.out" 2>"$WORK/leak.err"
  rc_leak=$?
  totals_leak="$(grep -E '^  [0-9]+ passed, [0-9]+ failed, [0-9]+ skipped$' "$WORK/leak.out" | tail -1)"
  ok_leak="$(grep -c '^  ok ' "$WORK/leak.out")"
  fail_leak="$(grep -c '^  FAIL ' "$WORK/leak.out")"
  skip_leak="$(grep -c '^  skip ' "$WORK/leak.out")"
  ok_says_skipped="$(grep '^  ok ' "$WORK/leak.out" | grep -c 'skipped')"
  p_leak="$(printf '%s' "$totals_leak" | awk '{print $1}')"
  f_leak="$(printf '%s' "$totals_leak" | awk '{print $3}')"
  s_leak="$(printf '%s' "$totals_leak" | awk '{print $5}')"
  if [ -n "$totals_leak" ] && [ "$s_leak" -ge 1 ] \
     && [ "$p_leak" = "$ok_leak" ] && [ "$f_leak" = "$fail_leak" ] && [ "$s_leak" = "$skip_leak" ] \
     && [ "$ok_says_skipped" -eq 0 ] && [ "$rc_leak" -ne 0 ]; then
    ok "a leaked KS923_SELFTEST_CHILD makes the child print '$totals_leak' — parity with its ok/FAIL/skip lines, none disguised as ok — and exit non-zero (rc=$rc_leak)"
  else
    bad "a leaked KS923_SELFTEST_CHILD is COUNTED on the totals line (passed/failed/skipped == ok/FAIL/skip lines) and fails the exit code" \
        "rc=$rc_leak; totals line: '${totals_leak:-<no line with a skipped counter>}' (last line: $(tail -1 "$WORK/leak.out")); ok lines=$ok_leak, FAIL lines=$fail_leak, skip lines=$skip_leak, ok-lines-saying-skipped=$ok_says_skipped"
  fi
fi

# KS-941 QA-923-2 — the third counter, so the totals cannot claim a cell that
# did not run. A skipped cell also FAILS the exit code (STANDING_LINES rule 2,
# ruled for KS-941 on 2026-09-13): a run that could not execute part of itself
# has not passed. Safe because the only way to reach a skip is the recursion
# guard leaking in from outside — the legitimate self-test child exits 2 at the
# ORCH_SH guard above before any cell runs, so it never reaches this line.
printf '\n  %d passed, %d failed, %d skipped\n' "$pass" "$fail" "$skipped"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
[ "$skipped" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
exit 0
